messages: /tokenwise:route implement a feature from a written spec, about 12 files
/tokenwise:route review a six-file diff in a repo I know well

result:
- **Phase:** Implement a feature from a written spec, about 12 files.
- **Model and effort:** `/model sonnet` then `/effort medium`. On the bench, sonnet at medium passed every run at 17% of the cost of opus at xhigh. That result is for `claude-sonnet-5` on a small test project, so a 12-file feature is bigger than anything it tested. If `sonnet` points to a newer model for you, the evidence still comes from `claude-sonnet-5`.
- **Boundary:** Run `/clear` first, switch model and effort, then start from the spec file. If you switch without clearing, your whole current context gets re-processed on the new model. `/context` shows how big that is. This answer stays in your context until your next `/clear`, so routing just before one costs least. If the session gets long partway through, write progress into the spec's task list, `/clear`, and pick up from the file.
- **Delegate:** Set `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL=haiku` and `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE=1` (needs Claude Code 2.1.257 or later). Hand subagents the reading of the existing code the spec touches, plus test runs and log reading, so only summaries come back. Keep the edits in the main session.
- **Done when:** Tests and lint pass, and `git diff --stat` shows no existing test file was edited.
- **You give up:** At medium, sonnet makes fewer tool calls and thinks less. It will build the spec as written and is less likely to flag gaps, or places where the 12 files have to agree in ways the spec doesn't spell out. Settle any open questions in the spec before you start.
- **Escalate when:**
  - **It skipped files, didn't run the tests, or stopped mid-task:** stay on sonnet and raise to `/effort high`, then `xhigh`. On the bench, sonnet at xhigh cost less per completed task than opus at medium.
  - **It read the relevant code and still got a spec item wrong:** after a `/clear`, switch to `/model opus` at `medium`, then `xhigh`.
  - **The spec itself turns out to be ambiguous:** that's planning work. Use opus at `high`, fix the spec file, then come back to implementation.

- **Phase:** Review a six-file diff in a familiar repo.
- **Model and effort:** `/model opus` then `/effort low`. The bench ran this exact case: a six-file diff with five planted defects. Opus at low effort found all five in 3 turns. Opus at high found the same five in 13 turns and cost 3.3x as much. That evidence is from `claude-opus-5` as it resolved on 8 September 2026. If `opus` points to a newer model for you, the row describes the older one.
- **Boundary:** If you're changing model, run `/clear` first. The switch is then free. Switching on a warm context re-processes your whole current context, and `/context` shows how big that is. This answer also stays in your context until your next `/clear`, so routing just before one costs least.
- **Delegate:** Nothing by default, because six files fit in the main context. If the review needs test runs, or callers outside the diff read, send those to a subagent. With `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL=haiku` and `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE=1` set, that reading runs on Haiku and only the summary comes back.
- **Done when:** Every finding carries a file:line and an input that makes it fail, and all six files have been read. A review that returns no findings should still name each of the six files it covered.
- **You give up:**
  - Low effort makes fewer tool calls and does less tracing into code outside the diff.
  - Knowing the repo covers most of that, since you can spot a missed interaction yourself.
  - Sonnet would cost less, but at high effort it missed one of the five defects in two runs out of three.
- **Escalate when:**
  - **A file got skipped, a finding wasn't checked against the code, or it stopped early:** raise effort with `/effort high`.
  - **It had the right files and still got the code wrong:** a false finding, or a defect you can point to that it read past. Change model with `/model fable`.
  - **The diff turns out bigger or reaches into code you don't know:** `/effort high` on opus is the row's starting point for that.
